prints.name: The larger mat needs another revision.
prints.description: The accepted small sample became a 10.6 cm coaster by repeating the same links. The larger print has localized damaged links and tangled plastic, with fine threads across the mat. The owner confirms the damage was already present on the plate.
prints.estimateNote: Physical result documented by two owner photographs and feedback. Actual time and mass are unmeasured; printer completion was not independently checked. Photos show the outcome, not the sequence of failure. Thermal performance and mug stability remain untested.
prints.credit: Derived from Loop Link Fidget Fabric by Sean Liang / Starry Odyssey (seanliang00) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · starryodyssey.com/design/loop-link-fidget-fabric. Modified geometry prepared with Codex: broader feet, chamfered flat-bottomed bars, sloped hole roofs, increased pitch and thickness. This version repeats those links in a larger grid. Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality

Fine stringing and several areas of tangled extrusion or incomplete links are visible. The owner reports major flaws already present on the plate. This prototype is not accepted as a finished coaster.
Learned

A better 3×3 sample did not establish reliability across 225 parts. Local detachment or failed spans remain possible. The first crossbar layer also uses mixed cooling for its centre fill; that is a testable process weakness, not a confirmed cause.
Next time

Use a smaller diagnostic patch and observe the first feet and crossbar layers. Test consistent cooling across the crossbars while retaining the 215°C target and link geometry. Establish intact links before another full coaster; drying remains a separate stringing experiment.

photos.alt: Close-up of the lilac linked coaster with fine strings, localized tangled plastic and damaged-looking links.
photos.caption: The larger mat: fine stringing and several local areas of print damage.

photos.alt: Lilac linked coaster held at the edge, showing incomplete links and a clump of extruded plastic near the lower edge.
photos.caption: A second angle on the damaged area. The owner confirms these flaws were present before removal.

prints.name: Five degrees cooler. A better fabric.
prints.description: The same revised 3×3 patch, with the nozzle target reduced from 220°C to 215°C after the first layer. The owner reports a much better result and is ready to try a coaster-sized version. No photograph has been recorded for this sample yet.
prints.estimateNote: Completion and improvement are owner-reported, with completion also confirmed by printer status. Time and material retain the earlier slicer estimate because motion and extrusion commands were preserved; actual time and mass are unmeasured. Temperature ranges below are periodic samples, not continuous telemetry. No photo or quantified strength test was supplied.
prints.credit: Derived from Loop Link Fidget Fabric by Sean Liang / Starry Odyssey (seanliang00) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · starryodyssey.com/design/loop-link-fidget-fabric. Modified geometry prepared with Codex: broader feet, chamfered flat-bottomed bars, sloped hole roofs, increased pitch and thickness. Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
Owner reports “much much better” and accepts the result as a basis for a larger print. Improvement is qualitative; zero stringing and joint strength have not been established.
Learned

Only the nozzle target after layer 1 changed; geometry, extrusion paths, speeds and retraction were preserved. The improvement supports 215°C for this combination. In 26 printing samples, the nozzle read 214.8–215.3°C and the bed 64.9–65.1°C, with the intended targets and no reported errors.
Next time

Prepare a 10.6 cm square coaster by repeating the same links at their tested size. Check larger-area adhesion and mug stability. Open mesh will not catch spills; PLA heat resistance limits hot-mug use, so assess a cork contact surface before regular use.

prints.name: Better links. A few cobwebs.
prints.description: A smaller, rebuilt Loop Link sample with broader feet, flat-bottomed bars and sloped connector roofs. The owner reports a much better print, with fine cobweb-like threads still appearing between links. No photograph has been recorded for this sample yet.
prints.estimateNote: Completion and improvement are owner-reported. Actual time and mass are unmeasured. No photo or quantified movement/strength test was supplied. The subsequent 215°C comparison is recorded in its own entry.
prints.credit: Derived from Loop Link Fidget Fabric by Sean Liang / Starry Odyssey (seanliang00) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · starryodyssey.com/design/loop-link-fidget-fabric. Modified geometry prepared with Codex: broader feet, chamfered flat-bottomed bars, sloped hole roofs, increased pitch and thickness. Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
Owner reports a much better completed print, with fine cobweb-like threads between links. Free movement, strength and close-up surface quality have not yet been assessed.
Learned

The small revised patch improved the reported outcome, but several geometry and process variables changed together. Fine threads are consistent with stringing; their exact cause is unconfirmed. Retraction and wiping were already enabled.
Next time

Follow-up: the same toolpaths were printed with a 215°C nozzle target after the 220°C first layer. The owner reports a much better result; the separate temperature-comparison entry records the outcome.

prints.name: A fabric sample that came loose.
prints.object: Loop Link Fidget Fabric · failed first attempt
prints.description: The first 8×8 Loop Link sample in lilac, printed at the creator’s original scale. Several links detached or moved and extrusion tangled around the damaged area. The job was stopped before completion; it is not a usable fabric sample.
prints.estimateNote: Time and material are estimates for the complete planned print, not the failed attempt’s consumption. Actual elapsed time and mass are unmeasured. The owner’s photograph records the failure before stopping; the public copy has metadata removed, with defects preserved.
prints.credit: Model: Sean Liang / Starry Odyssey (seanliang00), Loop Link Fidget Fabric · CC BY-SA 4.0 · starryodyssey.com/design/loop-link-fidget-fabric. Original 8×8 geometry at 100% scale. Photo by Huzaifa. Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
Failed. The photo shows displaced links, missing portions of the grid and tangled filament. The printer was still running at layer 9/25; stopping was confirmed and both heater targets turned off.
Learned

The model starts on 368 small contact pads. A valid toolpath and a reported first layer do not prove adhesion. Loss of adhesion is the leading explanation, but the photo cannot establish whether lifting or a nozzle catch happened first. Plate contamination is not proven.
Next time

Follow-up: the plate was washed and a smaller, rebuilt 3×3 patch was printed with broader feet and gentler motion. The owner reports a much better result, with some fine stringing; the separate revised-sample entry records that outcome.

photos.alt: Failed lilac Loop Link fabric on the textured printer plate, with displaced links, missing grid sections and tangled filament beneath the print head
photos.caption: Failed first attempt · displaced links and tangled extrusion

prints.name: A little heart, folded in pink.
prints.description: Sean Liang’s origami-inspired heart box, assembled at original size in Sakura Pink. The patterned folding lids and textured box were printed in two separate high-quality jobs; the finished assembly is shown closed from three angles.
settings: 14 h 5 min 37 sec · summed slicer estimates
prints.estimateNote: Date marks the assembled-photo and fit report. Totals cover the two selected 0.12 mm print jobs; actual time and mass are unmeasured. Cooling, assembly and extra startup purge may add time or material. Photos are cropped around the box and metadata stripped, without retouching. The monitor is excluded from the handheld photo.
prints.credit: Model: Sean Liang / Starry Odyssey (seanliang00), Origami Heart Box · CC BY-SA 4.0 · starryodyssey.com/design/origami-heart-box. Original geometry at 100% scale. Photos by Huzaifa. Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality

Photos show the assembled pink box with both lids closed, the handle fitted, and the lid and wall patterns visible. Layer texture remains visible. Full opening/closing smoothness has not yet been reported.
Learned
Four pieces of 1.75 mm filament act as hinge axles for the folding lids. The initial handle-seating concern was resolved during assembly; no geometry change was reported.
Next time
Check a few gentle full opening/closing cycles for free hinge motion and handle clearance, then record the mechanism open.

prints.name: A tiny spiral, with a little friction.
prints.description: A lilac spiral passes through an ivory ring with a twisting slide. Sean Liang designed it as a small capsule toy. The original two components were separated without resizing, then printed sequentially: short ivory ring first, tall lilac spiral second. That gave two contrasting colors with just one filament change.
prints.material: Ivory White & Lilac Purple PLA Matte
settings: None / none; original ring includes a modeled centre bar
prints.estimateNote: Date marks the photo and handling report; the print finished October 10 at all 343 layer events without reported errors. Actual mass and duration are unmeasured; startup purge may add material. Photos are cropped to the fidget and metadata stripped, with no retouching. The desk photograph clips the spiral tip in the original.
prints.credit: Model: Sean Liang / Starry Odyssey (seanliang00), Tiny Spiral Passthrough Fidget · CC BY-SA 4.0 · thingiverse.com/thing:7354874. Original geometry preserved at 100% scale; parts separated for printing. Photos by Huzaifa. Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality

The owner says it is good and works, though the slide is not the smoothest and makes a slight sound. Photos show the assembled ivory ring and lilac spiral, with visible texture on the spiral. Sliding force and noise were not measured.
Learned

In an October 17 follow-up, the owner reported that removing the solid crossbar inside the sliding ring makes its motion rough. Source inspection found a 2 mm-thick bar built into the ring, so disabling generated supports does not remove it. Cutting damage is a possible cause of the roughness, not a confirmed diagnosis.
Next time

Test a replacement ring with the modeled centre bar omitted, retaining the original outer dimensions, curved guide shape and 0.16 mm process. This avoids cutting inside the opening and isolates one design change. The revision is prepared but has not yet been printed or physically tested.

prints.name: A starship, caught on the desk.
prints.description: From a cute rocket to a slender starship: a pointed nose and contrasting curved shield give the silhouette its character, while a rear opening keeps two pens accessible. Mirrored hull ledges rest on fixed lavender catch arms. Two white lattice panels print flat and assemble into a tower. Four separate color batches avoid repeated color changes within a print, at the cost of more assembly and glued decorations.
prints.estimateNote: Date marks the assembled-photo report. Totals cover the four final plates, including generated supports and brims; they exclude the earlier 30.74 g joint test and extra startup purge. Actual mass and elapsed time are unmeasured. Four printed fins are not visible in these assembly views. Photos show two pens at rest, not a measured handling or stability test.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s direction and iterative feedback. Inspired by Starship and its catch tower; a stylized desk object, not a scale replica. Photos by Huzaifa. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality

The owner calls it “glorious.” Photos show the assembled tower, ship held above the base, two pens in the rear bay, and the pink nameplate and engine detail. Layer lines and a vertical line on the green shield remain visible. Exact joint gaps and glue placement are unmeasured.
Learned

The small connector test supported keeping the joint geometry, but its supported hull-ledge underside needed cleanup. In slicing, “supports enabled” was insufficient: build-plate-only supports missed the shield opening. Allowing supports on the model produced the required scaffold. Review actual toolpaths and keep bearing faces flat during cleanup; appearance, contact fit and retention are separate checks.
Next time

Keep the rear pen bay and mirrored catch contacts. Check repeated pen insertion/removal and gentle knocks on a flat surface. Trial support-interface changes on another small ledge sample before a full reprint; document the four fins once fitted. These are follow-up checks, not reported failures.

photos.caption: Tower assembly · two flat-printed lattice panels

photos.caption: Close detail · surface texture and engine clearance

prints.name: One piece. A decent fit.
prints.description: The successful frame, contact-cap and tilt-riser experiment became one fixed angular stand with mirrored handle supports and an open chevron base. The owner reports that the print went well and the controller now sits decently well. Photos will follow.
prints.estimateNote: Date shown is the owner’s result-report date; the exact completion date and actual print time are unrecorded. Completion and decent seating are owner-reported. Photos, exact contact area and resistance to cable pulls are not yet documented. Time and mass are slicer estimates, not measured totals.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s measurements and iterative feedback. Controller: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
The owner reports that the print went well and the controller sits decently well. Surface finish and detailed contact cannot yet be assessed from photos.
Learned

The working assembly’s mirrored contact layout survived integration into one piece. Lowering all contact centres equally by 8 mm preserved their relative positions; the upper face separately received the reviewed 2° change.
Next time
Review the promised photos for grip seating, upper-shell contact and clearances. Check cable access and response to ordinary handling before deciding whether another fit refinement is worthwhile.

prints.name: The tilt that made it settle.
prints.description: A rear-foot riser tilts the existing frame and contact cap together by 30°. The owner reports that the controller now settles downward toward the handle supports. This successful trial supplies the geometry for a cleaner, integrated stand.
prints.estimateNote: Completion and successful forward settling are owner-reported and accompanied by photos of the finished assembly. Time and material are estimates for the riser alone, excluding the earlier frame and cap. Exact contact area and resistance to cable pulls are unmeasured.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s measurements and iterative feedback. Controller: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality

The supplied photos show the completed riser supporting the assembled cradle. The owner reports that forward/downward settling now works; the upper contact could still benefit from a slightly flatter face.
Learned

Tilting the whole fixture changed the direction it encouraged the controller to move while retaining the existing contact profiles. A useful contact shape and a useful overall orientation are separate design choices.
Next time

Integrate the successful geometry into one angular, open stand with mirrored handle supports. Test an upper contact about 2° flatter while preserving the overall tilt. The integrated revision is planned, not yet printed.

prints.name: A small test. A bigger rethink.
prints.description: A small slip-on test cap tried a raised, re-angled upper contact on the existing frame. It printed successfully, but the owner reports that the controller still slides backward and down. The retention experiment failed.
prints.estimateNote: The printer reported completion at 133 layers without errors. Time and material are slicer estimates, not measured totals. The owner reports the sliding; the photographs show the installed cap, with a hand present, and do not measure force, contact pressure or exact gaps.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s measurements and iterative feedback. Controller: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
The printed cap appears intact in the supplied photos, but it does not retain the controller: backward and downward slipping persists. Cap seating and exact contact area remain unmeasured.
Learned

A taller post does not guarantee a forward seating force. The cap’s main face still descends toward USB-C, and the front lips cannot catch motion in the opposite direction. Matching a contour is not the same as providing retention.
Next time

Test tilting the whole existing cradle before printing again. Develop mirrored handle pockets with front and rear stops, keeping upward removal and charging access clear. This redesign is planned, not printed.

photos.alt: Side view of the controller, test cap and original handle cradle, with a hand beside the stand

prints.name: Better seating. More to refine.
prints.description: The revised frame is one fixed piece with mirrored grip cradles and a rear ramp that rises toward USB-C. The owner reports a much better fit at the handles, but only narrow line contact at the upper support.
prints.estimateNote: The printer reported completion at all 220 layers without errors; supplied photos confirm the physical print. Time and mass are slicer estimates, not measured totals. Photographs show contact regions from oblique angles; exact gaps, controller tilt and contact pressure are not measured.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s measurements and iterative feedback. Controller: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality

The owner reports that the handles now sit pretty well. The upper support touches fixed shell but still makes narrow line contact, with an apparent gap in the photos; other reported problems await clarification.
Learned

The mirrored grips seat better. Upper-post height sets the supported pose, while its face angle controls local contact; changing one does not settle the other. The photographed frame straddles a mat edge, so retest on one flat surface.
Next time

Preserve the handles and one-piece design. The gap cannot be measured, so the next draft uses an explicitly assumed earlier profile and a modest added tilt. Test the contact and retention physically; the draft has not been printed.

prints.name: A fit test that changed the design.
prints.description: The first printed frame reached its real test: holding the controller. It did not retain it reliably. The owner reports backward slipping; the hand-held photos document the contact areas rather than a stable resting position.
prints.estimateNote: Printed specimen confirmed by the owner and photos. Date records the fit review. Settings and estimates come from the saved print package; actual weight and duration were not measured. Startup purge can add material. Photo perspective does not establish exact gaps or tilt.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s measurements and feedback. Controller: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
The printed frame appears intact, but the functional fit failed: the controller slides backward. Photos show uneven seating; exact gaps and dimensional accuracy are unmeasured.
Learned
Fitting two supports independently to a rough scan introduced a 2.63 mm difference at their centres. Agreement with that scan did not prove correct seating or retention.
Next time
Test mirrored shallow grip cradles and a rear ramp that rises toward the USB-C end. A removable block and 2 mm spacers are planned for height adjustment; the revision has not been printed.

prints.name: A little character. A lot of heart.
prints.description: Our first original ornament: two rounded characters, recessed eyes and a softly rounded heart on a shared base. The first physical prototype follows several rounds of design refinement.
prints.estimateNote: Completed, as reported by the owner. Settings are from the saved print package; size is from CAD, not a physical measurement. Material includes generated supports; extra startup purge may add to it. Actual weight, duration, base flatness and joint strength have not been measured or tested.
prints.credit: Original model: designed in OpenSCAD by Codex with Huzaifa’s direction and iterative feedback. · Printed on the Bambu Lab A1.
notes: Quality
Photos show clean rounded bodies and readable eyes and ears. Visible terraces on the feet, fine wisps and rough spots around the arm and heart tip still need attention.
Learned
Even 0.16 mm layers leave steps on shallow curves. Raising the heart tip preserved its silhouette, but added a delicate area needing supports and careful cleanup.
Next time
Remove remaining wisps and support nubs gently. Test finer or adaptive layers on a small sample, then review seam placement and support contacts before a refined reprint.

prints.name: One boat. Two beginnings.
prints.description: The last of the white sample became the beginning of another boat. A filament-runout pause let us continue with the new gray PLA.
prints.estimateNote: Slicer estimates exclude the extended changeover pause and extra loading/purge material. No photograph was recorded for this print.
prints.credit: Model: 3DBenchy by Creative Tools. · Printed from the printer’s bundled file.
notes: Quality
Completed successfully; the owner reports that it looks great. No photo inspection or strength test was performed.
Learned
The runout sensor paused at layer 55. After manually loading gray PLA, the same job resumed; compatible PLA colors can bond as successive layers.
Next time
Inspect any restart boundary on functional parts. Use an uninterrupted print when comparing surface finish, so the pause is not another variable.

prints.name: A little tool, made here.
prints.description: The first useful print: a lightweight scraper, with a sloping blade that turned into a lesson about layers.
prints.estimateNote: Material and time are from the saved print file, not measurements. Loading and startup purge use extra filament.
prints.credit: Model: Bed scraper by JernejP. · Included with the printer.
notes: Quality
Sits flat without rocking. The openings look clean, and the underside has a consistent texture from the build plate.
Learned
A sloping surface becomes tiny terraces when printed in layers. At 0.20 mm, those steps are easy to see across the blade.
Next time
Print the same design at 0.10 mm and compare the blade. Keep the material, orientation and physical shell thickness comparable.

prints.name: Every adventure needs a boat.
prints.description: The little white boat that started it all. Our first finished print, after setup, calibration and learning to load filament.
prints.estimateNote: Filament use is an approximate owner estimate. Layer height and print duration have not been verified for this job.
prints.credit: Model: 3DBenchy by Creative Tools. · Printed from the printer’s bundled file.
notes: Quality
The boat sits flush. Photos show a complete hull and cabin, with a few fine wisps of stringing around the openings.
Learned
Loading is complete when melted filament actually exits the nozzle—not just when the strand reaches the guide tube.
Next time
Keep this boat as a baseline. Inspect fine strands and the roof under consistent lighting before changing settings.
